name: Storm Sabine
description: Overnight, a cold front linked to storm Sabine (Ciara) brought gusts of 85–125 km/h on the northern plains and 130–200 km/h on mountain peaks. In the south, stormy foehn winds blew with gusts of 50–70 km/h at low elevations, peaking at 90 km/h.

name: Severe Hailstorm in Locarno
description: This large-scale rain event was caused by a southwesterly flow. Warnings were issued by forecasters from all regional centers, partially for 48h precipitation accumulations and partially for 72h accumulations. In the region of Locarno, the event led to disproportionally large impacts because it was preceded by a violent hail storm on the evening of Aug 25.

name: Level 3 Heat
description: First heatwave in 2025 with particularly intense daily maximum temperatures. North of the Alps maxima reached 31–33 °C, up to 35.6 °C at Geneva, and thunderstorms from 30 June lowered the temperatures, especially in Valais.

name: Storm Benjamin
description: Storm “Benjamin” hit the north side of the Swiss Alps from Thursday into Friday, bringing strong west-winds with gusts up to about 90 km/h in the lowlands and up to 120 km/h or more in elevated locations.

name: Diurnal Convection
description: Overnight, thunderstorms formed over the Jura and moved east, weakening toward the Alps. In the afternoon, storms hit Ticino and later the Bernese Jura/Solothurn, with local heavy rain up to 70 mm. Most cells died out over the Plateau, while evening storms popped up again in the Alps and south. Sunshine was limited (max 8–10 h in S Ticino, less elsewhere) with highs of 25–33 °C in the north and 28–31 °C in the south.

name: Storm Petra
description: Storm-force winds: 70–100 km/h in the lowlands, 80–110 km/h above 1000 m, 110–140 km/h above 2000 m. After Petra caused damage north of the Gotthard overnight, strong gusts are now hitting Ticino, uprooting trees in Locarno. Heavy snowfall above 800 m (5–15 cm, above 1400 m 10–30 cm, snow line 600–1400 m).

name: Heavy Precipitation
description: The active weather system moved northeast, easing heavy rain over central and eastern regions. Between Friday morning and Sunday afternoon, central Ticino saw 200–250 mm of rain, with 280–350 mm between Lavizzara and parts of the Verzasca. Near the Alpine crest in the south 140–200 mm fell, in the central and eastern Alps up to the Rhine Valley 90–140 mm, and in the Surselva up to 170 mm. The snow line stayed high at 3000–3500 m, dropping to 2300–1800 m only at the end of the event.

name: Thunderstorm system. Severe flooding event in the Mesolcina valley.
Heavy stormy precipitation in southern Ticino
Level 3 heavy thunderstorm precipitation
description: 12-hour rainfall totals reached up to 150 mm in the Locarno area and Val Verzasca, with peak hourly values exceeding 50 mm.

name: Level 3 Heat
description: Southwesterly flow brought very warm air of subtropical origin to Ticino. Max 30–35 °C, min 20–23 °C, humidity 35–45%. Thunderstorms mid-event did not break the heat; the event ended with a thunderstorm system.

name: Level 3 Heat
description: Short but intense heatwave over the Geneva region and central Valais. Measured max 32–36 °C, heat index above 90. Ended by a thunderstorm system arriving from France.

name: Level 3 Heat
description: High-pressure ridge brought several days of heat with maxima of 30–33 °C and nightly minima above 20 °C. A depression ended the event with cooler air and showers.

name: Rain event
description: Small hail reported in the Locarno area and Sottoceneri. Only a few rain gauges in the Lugano area reached level 2 thresholds over 12 hours. False level 2 alarm.

name: Snowfall event
description: Fresh snow accumulations of 20–35 cm (Motta Naluns 39 cm), with a strong gradient between the Austrian border ridge and the Inn valley. Samnaun reached level 3 accumulations, Zuoz overall level 2.

name: Snowfall event
description: Convective snowfall (cold drop aloft, unstable air mass) with very irregular accumulation distribution. Level 2 thresholds reached widely, locally level 3–4 at low elevations, with Bosco Gurin reaching level 5. Thresholds exceeded mainly above 1400 m. Only a slippery roads warning was issued; missed level 2 alert for 3 out of 4 regions.

name: Strong north wind
description: Pressure difference between Kloten and Lugano reached 11 hPa, with a strong N-NW jet stream aloft. 6 out of 12 regions reached level 2 tresholds (60 km/h)

name: Snowfall event
description: Snow accumulations up to 30 cm in Valposchiavo, 9–25 cm elsewhere.  4 regions reached level 3, 4 level 2, 1 missed level 2 (Verzasca)

name: North wind situation
description: North to northwesterly flow with gusts up to 70 km/h, only Camignolo exceeded the threshold. Pressure difference KLO–LUG up to 11 hPa.

name: North wind situation
description: North foehn with gusts mostly below 60 km/h in ticino and Moesano. Only Poschiavo (non-alerted) reached 72 km/h.

name: Wind event on alpine ridge
description: Gusts mostly below level 2 thresholds at stations above 1600 m; only Piz Corvatsch station reached 94 km/h.

name: Level 3 and 2 snowfall event
description:
Two consecutive snowfall events. The first 

Event developed in a cold air mass with snow line at 500–600 m, intermittent and showery; a few cm below 600 m, 5–10 cm above, locally 10–15 cm in mountains. The second was associated with a warm front from the southeast, more widespread but with snow line at 900–1000 m dropping to 600 m.

name: Level 3 snowfall event
description: Warm front followed by a cold front associated with depression Chandra, with southwesterly flow conveying moist air toward the southern Alps. Snow line at 600–700 m, temporarily dropping to 300–400 m, then rising to 800–1200 m. Up to 40 cm in the Bernina region, 10–15 cm above 1000–1200 m.

name: Level 3 snowfall event
description: Depression over western Europe with southwesterly flow and blocking on the southern Alps, warm front and secondary trough with jet support. Snow line at 500–600 m, 15–20 cm above 800 m, 5–15 cm between 500–800 m, a few cm at low elevations.

name: Level 3-4 snowfall event
description: Stationary frontal system separating cold polar air from warm Mediterranean air, with southwesterly flow. Snow line dropped from above 1000 m to 500–700 m in Sopraceneri valleys, reaching the plains overnight. Up to 80–120 cm above 1500 m between Valle Maggia and Valle Verzasca; 50–80 cm between 1000–1500 m in western regions; 20–25 cm at 600–800 m in Locarnese. New 24h record at Bosco Gurin (116 cm). Avalanche activity and forest damage reported.

name: Level 3-4 Heat
description: High pressure with subtropical southwesterly air brought maximum temperatures widely of 33–35 °C, up to 35.5 °C (BIA), with minimum temperatures at low elevations above 20 °C and up to 25.3 °C (LUG). The heat ended with showers and thunderstorms

name: Level 3 Heat
description: A north foehn with high pressure, persisting longer than expected, kept maximum temperatures at 33–35 °C, up to 37.4 °C (OTL), and with dry air and limited nocturnal cooling kept minimum temperatures high. The heat ended as thunderstorms brought a drop in temperatures.

name: Level 3-4 Heat
description: High pressure over central and eastern Europe brought a new rise in temperatures, with very dry soils adding to the heat. Maximum temperatures frequently exceeded 33–35 °C, peaking at 39.2 °C in Biasca, the highest value of summer 2026 south of the Alps, while minimum temperatures reached up to 24.4 °C in Lugano. Daily mean temperatures stayed at or above 25 °C for 20 consecutive days in Lugano and 21 in Locarno-Monti, new all-time records for both stations, and the event is considered the longest and most intense heatwave in their measurement series, exceeding August 2003. Evening thunderstorms brought only temporary relief, and the event ended with a spell of unsettled weather that brought a clear drop in temperatures, with maxima no longer above 23–24 °C.

name: Level 3 Severe thunderstorms
description: Southwesterly flow brought very warm and humid air from the Po Valley to the south side of the Alps. Thunderstorms began in the evening with small hail and a gust of 97.2 km/h (MAG), then continued through the next day, with 67.2 mm in one hour, 44.8 mm in 30 minutes and 247.3 mm in 48 hours (BRA)

name: Level 3 stormy north wind
description: A cold front crossed the country from northwest, followed by polar air from the north that created a pressure difference of up to 14.5 hPa between Kloten and Lugano. Gusts reached 80–100 km/h widely in both lowlands and mountains, with 115.9 km/h at Monte Generoso and 95.8 km/h at Magadino/Cadenazzo, causing fallen trees and damage to infrastructure.

name: Severe hailstorm in Mendrisiotto
description: A supercell moved from the lower Lake Maggiore to the Mendrisiotto, producing hail of 2–5 cm, up to 4–5 cm at Castel S. Pietro and Morbio Superiore, and 40.9 mm of rain in 10 minutes at Coldrerio.

name: Long intense rain event
description: A cold front from west stalled over the region with a low pressure area aloft, and rain and thunderstorms regenerated in several phases over three days. 48-hour accumulations were 100–150 mm in central and southern Ticino, with peaks above 200 mm. Hourly maxima reached 51.6 mm at Crana-Torricella and 42.8 mm at Mosogno. The models put the heaviest rain in the wrong place, ICON-CH1/2-EPS too far north and ECMWF-IFS too far west, and warnings were issued for level 2 while the observed accumulations reached level 4 between the Sottoceneri and the Basso Moesano.

name: Heavy precipitation
description: Mild air from southwest and a cold front from northwest brought heavy rain on the west and north side of the Alps, both from the front and from the air rising against the mountains. The zero degree level fell from above 2400 m to 1500 m during the event. ICON forecast slightly too little rain on the Plateau and too much on the mountains.

name: Level 4 Heavy precipitation (ex-hurricane Erin)
description: A depression off Ireland, the former hurricane Erin, and a secondary low over the Gulf of Genoa drove humid southwesterly air towards the Alps, with cold fronts arriving from northwest. The heaviest rain fell in the Locarnese, Vallemaggia and the Sopraceneri valleys, with 12-hour totals of 120–180 mm, 184 mm at Mosogno and 147 mm at Cevio, while Stabio measured 203.6 mm in 48 hours. North of the Alps the rain came in two thunderstorm waves, and the models clearly overestimated the amounts on both sides.

name: Storm Amy
description: Storm Amy passed over northwestern Europe from Friday to Saturday, hitting the British Isles and northern France first, and reached the north side of the Swiss Alps on Saturday with a cold front and a marked temperature drop. Gusts reached 60–80 km/h in the lowlands, up to 100 km/h in exposed locations and 141 km/h on the Chasseral. Rain amounted to 2–10 mm in the lowlands and 10–30 mm on the northern slope of the Alps, with the snow line down to about 1500 m.

name: Level 4 Heavy Precipitation and Snowfall
description: A low named Hans over the Gulf of Genoa brought very humid air against the Alps from the south. Rainfall broke daily records in Valais and the Bernese Oberland, with 127 mm at Visp, 124 mm at Kandersteg and 119 mm at Leukerbad, and return periods above 100 years at some stations. A cold front from west and precipitation cooling brought the snow line down to the valley floors, with 30 cm of fresh snow at Visp, 9 cm at Sion and 100 cm at the Grand-St-Bernard pass.

name: Warm spell
description: High pressure brought widely sunny conditions in Switzerland. On 29 and 30 April maximum temperatures reached 23 to above 25 °C on both sides of the Alps, on 30 April locally around 26 °C in the north and 26 to almost 27 °C in the south. On both days showers and thunderstorms formed in the Alps from the afternoon.

name: Level 2 Heat event
description: Short hot spell at low elevations, with maxima of 30–35 °C (34.8 °C in Biasca) and minima of 14–22 °C. Daily mean temperatures exceeded 25 °C widely on only two days. Less warm, dry air from the east then lowered temperatures, without showers.

name: Level 2 Rain event
description: Convective rain with thunderstorms in two phases, the second with a cold front. Totals were very irregular, up to 76 mm in 12 hours and 102 mm in 18 hours, with the Bellinzona, Lugano and Mendrisio areas most affected.

name: Level 2 rain event
description: Level 2 amounts were widely exceeded in the Lugano and Bellinzona areas, the Riviera and the St. Moritz region, with up to 81 mm in 12 hours and level 3 amounts toward Val Morobbia.

name: Thunderstorm event
description: The passage was faster than forecast: thunderstorms started already in the early afternoon in the Alps, and later only a few local storms formed. Gusts reached 84 km/h at Locarno-Monti, with no damage reported.

description: Rain over Bregaglia, Poschiavo and the Engadin, with 12-hour totals up to 97 mm and 36-hour totals up to 125 mm. In the Engadin, 12-hour amounts reached level 3.

description: A fairly fast-moving weather system from the west brought 12-hour totals up to 92 mm, with the Lugano area reaching level 3 amounts.
